name: Numbers & time
description: Counting, prices, hours, and days. Hear them fast at the register.

cards.tip: Sino-Japanese number, used for counting, prices, time. Changes sound before some counters: ippun, issai.
Two. Also the particle ni (to, at); context separates them.
Three. Also the polite name suffix (Tanaka-san). sanbyaku = 300 with a sound change.
yon and shi both mean four; shi also means death, so yon is preferred in most counting.
Five. Also the honorific prefix on some words (gohan, gochisou). Context decides.
Six. roppyaku = 600, rokusen = 6000.
nana and shichi both mean seven; nana is clearer in speech because shichi sounds like ichi.
Eight. happyaku = 800, hassen = 8000. The small tsu stop appears before h and p sounds.
kyuu and ku both mean nine; kyuu is standard, ku shows up in time (kuji = 9 o'clock).
Ten. Tens stack: nijuu = 20, sanjuu = 30. juuichi = 11.
Hundred. Sound changes: sanbyaku (300), roppyaku (600), happyaku (800).
Thousand. sanzen (3000), hassen (8000). 1000 is just sen, not issen.

examples.ja: 一万円札しかありません。
examples.en: I only have a 10,000 yen note.

cards.tip: Ten thousand is the big unit: ichiman (10,000), juuman (100,000), hyakuman (one million). Prices are quoted in man.
Native Japanese counting (hitotsu to tou) counts generic things when there is no special counter. It follows the noun: kore o hitotsu.
Two things. Compare futari (two people) and ni (the bare number).
Three things. Note the stop: mit-tsu.
nan (what) + ji (hour counter). Answer: number + ji. Minutes use fun or pun.
san + ji = 3 o'clock. Four is yoji (not yonji), seven is shichiji, nine is kuji.
Today. Time nouns stand alone, no particle needed: kyou ikimasu.

examples.romaji: ashita wa nani o shimasu ka.

cards.tip: Tomorrow. asatte = the day after tomorrow. ashita no asa = tomorrow morning.
Yesterday, long o: kinou. Pairs with past tense: kinou ikimashita.
Now. ima kara = from now. Adverb, no particle.
ato (after) + de. ato de = later. X no ato de = after X.
nanji + ni (at, for clock times) + shimarimasu (close, intransitive) + ka. Opening is akimasu.
